title: Payment 5xx spike after payment-service deploy — revenue path affected

ground_truth.summary: Deploy v3.4.0 to payment-service introduced a null-dereference in the card-tokenization path; only /pay endpoints fail. refund-service (which also calls the external card-processor but did NOT receive the deploy) stays healthy — this proves the fault is the deploy, not the external processor. Rollback of v3.4.0 is the correct fix. Distinct from INC-4475 by service (payment vs checkout) and blast radius (P0 revenue path).

observables.name: sibling_service_errors
observables.desc: refund-service error rate (shares external-card-processor, did NOT get the deploy)

observables.name: error_type_breakdown
observables.desc: payment-service errors grouped by exception class

customer_impact.impact_source: payment-service POST /pay — direct revenue path, customer cannot complete checkout
customer_impact._note_for_authors: Highest-CIS bundle in the corpus. SLA 99.95% availability + p95 < 2000ms both breached. 25k affected users during the 18-minute window.

seed_hypotheses.claim: The 14:16 deploy v3.4.0 introduced a null-dereference in card tokenization and broke payment; roll it back.

predicted_observations.note: if the deploy is the cause, only payment-service should fail; refund-service (no deploy) should be fine

seed_hypotheses.claim: The external card-processor is degraded and is failing every caller regardless of deploy.

predicted_observations.note: refund-service also uses the processor and should fail too if the processor is at fault

prior._note_for_authors: External processor is HEALTHY from prior — flat p95 latency, well under threshold. Makes the processor-degradation story (H2) unlikely from prior; the sibling probe is the clean confirmation.

payload.signature: null-dereference introduced by deploy, single service 5xx
payload.resolution: Rolled back the offending deploy; errors cleared immediately.

probeable._note_for_authors: THE DISCRIMINATOR. refund-service shares the external-card-processor but did NOT get the deploy. It stays healthy (<0.3%). That is impossible if the processor were at fault (H2) — it confirms the deploy (H1). rollback_correct=true hinges on this.

Distractor probe: all errors are NullPointer (consistent with H1) but the seed hypotheses don't make opposing predictions on error_type_breakdown, so its info-gain is 0 — the mechanism should skip it and pick P_sibling.
